subject: Physics
title: Maximum Height of a Projectile
formula: H = (u² · sin²θ) / (2g)
variables: u = Initial launch velocity (m/s), θ = Angle of projection (°), g = Acceleration due to gravity (9.8 or 10 m/s²)
golden_trap: Students frequently square the angle instead of squaring sin(θ) [i.e., (sin θ)² NOT sin(θ²)]. Also do NOT confuse with Time of Flight formula.
mnemonic: Height needs High denominator (2g), Range has single g.
worked_example: A projectile is launched at 20 m/s at 30° to the horizontal. H = (20² × (0.5)²) / (2 × 10) = (400 × 0.25) / 20 = 100 / 20 = 5.0 meters.

subject: Physics
title: Total Time of Flight (Projectile)
formula: T = (2u · sinθ) / g
variables: u = Initial velocity, θ = Angle of projection, g = Acceleration due to gravity
golden_trap: Forgetting the factor of 2! Time to reach max height is u·sinθ/g; total time to return to ground is DOUBLE that.
mnemonic: Flight is Two-Way: Up and Down = Factor of 2.

subject: Physics
title: Horizontal Range (Projectile)
formula: R = (u² · sin(2θ)) / g
variables: u = Initial velocity, θ = Angle of projection, g = Acceleration of gravity
golden_trap: Using 2·sinθ instead of sin(2θ). Max range is ALWAYS achieved at θ = 45° because sin(2 × 45°) = sin(90°) = 1.
mnemonic: Range reaches farthest at 45 degrees, where sin(2θ) peaks at 1.

subject: Physics
title: Lens & Mirror Equation
variables: f = Focal length (m or cm), u = Object distance, v = Image distance
golden_trap: Sign convention error! For convex lens / concave mirror, f is POSITIVE. For concave lens / convex mirror, f is NEGATIVE. Real images have positive v; virtual images have negative v.
mnemonic: Real is Positive, Virtual is Negative (RIP VN).
worked_example: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens (f = +10 cm). 1/v = 1/10 - 1/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. v = +15 cm (Real, inverted image).

subject: Physics
title: Snell's Law of Refraction
formula: n₁ · sin(θ₁) = n₂ · sin(θ₂) => n = sin(i) / sin(r)
variables: n = Refractive index of medium, i = Angle of incidence, r = Angle of refraction
golden_trap: Measuring angles from the surface instead of the NORMAL line! Always measure angles to the normal perpendicular.
mnemonic: Angles love the Normal: Always measure to the normal line, never the boundary plane.
worked_example: Light enters water (n = 1.33) from air (n = 1) at incidence angle 30°. sin(r) = (1 × sin 30°) / 1.33 = 0.5 / 1.33 = 0.376. r ≈ 22.1°.

subject: Physics
title: De Broglie Matter Wavelength
formula: λ = h / p = h / (m · v)
variables: λ = Wavelength (m), h = Planck's constant (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s), p = Momentum (kg·m/s), m = Mass (kg), v = Velocity (m/s)
golden_trap: Forgetting to convert electron mass or velocity units to SI standard (kg and m/s).
mnemonic: Lambda Hates Heavy People: Heavy mass means imperceptibly tiny wavelength.
worked_example: An electron (m = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg) travels at 2.0 × 10⁶ m/s. λ = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ / (9.1 × 10⁻³¹ × 2.0 × 10⁶) = 3.64 × 10⁻¹⁰ meters.

subject: Physics
title: Radioactive Decay & Half-Life
formula: N = N₀ · (1/2)^(t / T_half)
variables: N = Remaining mass/atoms, N₀ = Initial mass/atoms, t = Elapsed time, T_half = Half-life duration
golden_trap: Confusing fraction remaining with fraction decayed! Fraction decayed = 1 - (Remaining / N₀).
mnemonic: Decay splits in half every step: 100% -> 50% -> 25% -> 12.5% -> 6.25%.
worked_example: A 80g sample has a half-life of 4 days. After 12 days (3 half-lives), remaining mass = 80 × (1/2)³ = 80 / 8 = 10 grams.

subject: Physics
title: Ohm's Law & Resistor Resistivity
formula: V = I · R  and  R = (ρ · L) / A
variables: V = Potential difference (Volts), I = Current (Amperes), R = Resistance (Ω), ρ = Resistivity (Ω·m), L = Length (m), A = Cross-sectional area (m² = πr²)
golden_trap: When a wire is stretched to double its length (L becomes 2L), its area halves (A becomes A/2), so resistance increases by a factor of 4 (2²)! Length doubles, Area halves.
mnemonic: Stretching quadruples: Double length = 4x resistance.
worked_example: A wire of resistance 5Ω is stretched to twice its length. New resistance = 5 × 2² = 20Ω.

subject: Physics
title: Ideal Electrical Transformer Equation
formula: V_p / V_s = N_p / N_s = I_s / I_p
variables: V = Voltage, N = Number of coil turns, I = Current, p = Primary coil, s = Secondary coil
golden_trap: Current ratio is INVERTED relative to voltage! Step-up voltage means step-down current (conservation of energy: P_in = P_out).
mnemonic: More Voltage = Less Current (P = V × I stays constant in ideal transformers).
worked_example: Primary turns = 500, Secondary turns = 100, V_p = 240V. V_s = 240 × (100 / 500) = 48V (Step-down).

subject: Physics
title: Heat Capacity & Latent Heat
formula: Q = m · c · ΔT  (Sensible heat)  and  Q = m · L  (Phase change)
variables: Q = Thermal energy (Joules), m = Mass (kg), c = Specific heat capacity (J/kg·K), ΔT = Temperature change, L = Specific latent heat (J/kg)
golden_trap: During a phase change (e.g. melting ice or boiling steam), temperature DOES NOT CHANGE (ΔT = 0). Never multiply L by ΔT!
mnemonic: Phase Change is Flat: No ΔT during melting or boiling, use Q = mL alone.
worked_example: Energy to melt 0.2 kg of ice at 0°C (L_f = 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg): Q = 0.2 × 3.36 × 10⁵ = 67,200 Joules.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ideal Gas Equation
formula: P · V = n · R · T
variables: P = Pressure (atm or Pa), V = Volume (L or m³), n = Moles (mol), R = Universal gas constant (0.0821 L·atm/mol·K or 8.314 J/mol·K), T = Absolute Temperature (MUST BE IN KELVIN)
golden_trap: FATAL JAMB TRAP: Forgetting to convert Celsius to Kelvin! T(K) = T(°C) + 273. Substituting °C guarantees an immediate zero.
mnemonic: Pure Virgin Never Refuses Tea (PV = nRT) — Always invited in KELVIN.
worked_example: 2 moles of gas at 27°C (300 K) and 1 atm occupies: V = (2 × 0.0821 × 300) / 1 = 49.26 Liters.

subject: Chemistry
title: Graham's Law of Gaseous Diffusion
formula: Rate₁ / Rate₂ = √(M₂ / M₁) = √(d₂ / d₁)
variables: Rate = Rate of diffusion (mL/s), M = Molar mass (g/mol), d = Vapor density
golden_trap: Inversion error! Rate of gas 1 is proportional to the square root of the molar mass of gas 2 on top! Lighter gases diffuse FASTER.
mnemonic: Lighter runs faster: Hydrogen (2) diffuses 4x faster than Oxygen (32) because √(32/2) = √16 = 4.
worked_example: Compare diffusion rates of CH₄ (M = 16) and SO₂ (M = 64): R(CH₄)/R(SO₂) = √(64/16) = √4 = 2. CH₄ diffuses twice as fast.

subject: Chemistry
title: Faraday's First Law of Electrolysis
formula: m = Z · I · t  =  (M · I · t) / (n · F)
variables: m = Mass deposited (g), I = Current (A), t = Time (seconds), M = Molar mass (g/mol), n = Number of electrons transferred, F = Faraday constant (96,500 C/mol)
golden_trap: Time MUST be in seconds! If JAMB gives time in minutes or hours, multiply by 60 or 3600 immediately.
mnemonic: Faraday likes Seconds: Minutes × 60, Hours × 3600.
worked_example: Current of 5A flows for 1930s through Cu²⁺ solution (M=64, n=2): m = (64 × 5 × 1930) / (2 × 96,500) = 617,600 / 193,000 = 3.2 grams.

subject: Chemistry
title: pH & pOH Calculations
formula: pH = -log₁₀[H⁺]  and  pH + pOH = 14
variables: [H⁺] = Hydrogen ion molarity (mol/dm³), [OH⁻] = Hydroxide ion concentration
golden_trap: For diprotic acids like H₂SO₄, [H⁺] is DOUBLE the molarity of the acid! 0.05M H₂SO₄ gives [H⁺] = 0.10M => pH = 1.0, NOT 1.3.
mnemonic: Count the Hydrogens: Diprotic doubles [H⁺]; Triprotic triples [H⁺].
worked_example: Solution with [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol/dm³ has pH = -log(10⁻⁴) = 4.0. Its pOH is 14 - 4 = 10.0.

subject: Chemistry
title: OIL RIG & Oxidation State Rules
formula: Oxidation = Loss of Electrons; Reduction = Gain of Electrons
variables: Reducing Agent = Gets oxidized (donates e⁻); Oxidizing Agent = Gets reduced (accepts e⁻)
golden_trap: The Reducing Agent is the substance whose oxidation number INCREASES. Students frequently mix up the agent with the process.
mnemonic: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain.
worked_example: In Zn + Cu²⁺ -> Zn²⁺ + Cu: Zn loses 2e⁻ (Oxidized, hence Zinc is the Reducing Agent). Cu²⁺ gains 2e⁻ (Reduced, hence Cu²⁺ is Oxidizing Agent).

subject: Mathematics
title: Quadratic Formula & Nature of Roots
formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a)  |  Discriminant D = b² - 4ac
variables: a, b, c = Coefficients of ax² + bx + c = 0; D > 0 (Real & distinct roots), D = 0 (Equal/repeated roots), D < 0 (Complex/imaginary roots)
golden_trap: Remember -b in front! If b is already negative (e.g. -5), -b becomes POSITIVE 5. Also remember to divide the entire numerator by 2a, not just the root.
mnemonic: Negative Boy couldn't decide (±) whether to go to a Radical party...

subject: Mathematics
title: Arithmetic Progression (A.P.)
variables: a = First term, d = Common difference (T₂ - T₁), n = Number of terms, S_n = Sum of first n terms
golden_trap: Using n instead of (n - 1) in the nth term formula. For the first term (n=1), (n-1)d = 0.
mnemonic: Step count is one less than term count: 10th step takes 9 jumps.

subject: Mathematics
title: Geometric Progression (G.P.) & Sum to Infinity
formula: T_n = a · r^(n-1)  and  S_∞ = a / (1 - r)  (where |r| < 1)
variables: a = First term, r = Common ratio (T₂ / T₁), S_∞ = Sum to infinity (only exists if -1 < r < 1)
golden_trap: Sum to infinity ONLY converges if common ratio magnitude is strictly less than 1 (|r| < 1). If r >= 1, sum diverges.
mnemonic: Infinite sum shrinks only when ratio is a proper fraction.

subject: Mathematics
title: Differentiation Rules (Chain, Product, Quotient)
formula: Product: (u·v)' = u'v + uv'  |  Quotient: (u/v)' = (u'v - uv') / v²
variables: u and v are differentiable functions of x
golden_trap: Quotient rule minus sign order! It is always (derivative of top × bottom) MINUS (top × derivative of bottom). Reversing signs ruins the derivative.
mnemonic: Low d-High minus High d-Low, over the square of what's below.
worked_example: Differentiate y = (x²)/(x + 1): Top u = x² (u' = 2x), Bottom v = x + 1 (v' = 1). dy/dx = [2x(x + 1) - x²(1)] / (x + 1)² = (x² + 2x) / (x + 1)².

subject: Mathematics
title: Trig Ratios & Sine/Cosine Rules
formula: Sine Rule: a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC  |  Cosine Rule: a² = b² + c² - 2bc·cosA
variables: a, b, c = Side lengths; A, B, C = Opposite interior angles
golden_trap: Use Sine rule when you know an angle and its opposite side. Use Cosine rule when you have two sides and the INCLUDED angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS).
mnemonic: SOH CAH TOA for right angles; Sine Rule for opposite pairs; Cosine Rule for SAS sandwiches.

subject: Economics
title: Price Elasticity of Demand (PED)
formula: PED = (% Change in Quantity Demanded) / (% Change in Price) = (ΔQ / Q₁) / (ΔP / P₁)
variables: ΔQ = Q₂ - Q₁, ΔP = P₂ - P₁, P₁ = Initial price, Q₁ = Initial quantity
golden_trap: Forgetting that PED is conventionally expressed in absolute value (|PED|). |PED| > 1 is Elastic, |PED| < 1 is Inelastic, |PED| = 1 is Unitary.
mnemonic: Demand on Top, Price at Bottom: Consumers react on top, Prices push from below.
worked_example: Price rises from ₦100 to ₦120 (+20%), quantity falls from 50 to 40 units (-20%). PED = |-20% / +20%| = 1.0 (Unitary elasticity).

subject: Biology
title: Mendelian Monohybrid Cross Ratio
formula: F₂ Phenotypic Ratio = 3:1  |  F₂ Genotypic Ratio = 1:2:1 (TT : Tt : tt)
variables: T = Dominant allele, t = Recessive allele; F₁ generation is heterozygous (Tt)
golden_trap: JAMB tricks candidates by asking for the GENOTYPIC ratio (1:2:1) when candidates automatically click 3:1 (the PHENOTYPIC ratio)! Read the question word carefully.
mnemonic: Phenotype is What you See (3 Tall : 1 Short); Genotype is the Gene Blueprint (1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt).
worked_example: Crossing two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt × Tt) gives 75% tall and 25% dwarf offspring.
